clue.text: Allow no one else to use the shampoo? Nonsense!

parts.words: Allow no one else to use
parts.note: to hog something is to keep it all to yourself
a shampoo is a hair wash

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps the shared shampoo to themselves is told they are talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the slangy sense of HOG, a verb for monopolising.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash is an informal word for rubbish talk, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Journalist covers social organisation in border town

indicators.note: covers means the outer word wraps round the inner one

parts.note: hack is a slang term for a journalist
WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women

explanation.surface: A reporter writes up a club in a frontier town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawick is a town in the Scottish Borders; the WI is Britain's Women's Institute.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawick lies in the Scottish Borders region, near the English border.

clue.text: Eventually sow border with last of seed, extremely reliable

parts.note: a gilt is a young female pig that will in time become a sow
an edge is a border

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions for sowing seed along a garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sow' reads as planting seed; it is the female pig, and a gilt grows into one.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilt-edged describes very safe investments, hence extremely dependable.

clue.text: Eagerly desiring to knock off good drug

indicators.note: to knock off means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: aspiring means eagerly wanting or ambitious

explanation.surface: Someone keen to get rid of a beneficial medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling drug.

clue.text: Architect designed washroom round back of block

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the single letter
designed suggests the letters are laid out to a new plan
back of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An architect drew up a washroom around the rear of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the fodder to HAWSMOOR before the K goes in. Nicholas Hawksmoor was an English baroque architect who worked with Wren.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Hawksmoor was an English baroque architect of London churches.

clue.text: In Russian city, long for living expenses

indicators.note: the opening word puts the second piece inside the city

parts.note: Perm is a city in the Urals
to be dying for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a Russian city pines for an allowance to live on.
explanation.definitionFit: A per diem is a daily allowance paid to cover living costs while working away.

clue.text: Nothing out of jug perhaps could be more clean

indicators.note: out of means the letter is taken from the longer word

parts.note: a jug is an example of a pourer, a vessel for pouring
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: An empty jug might count as cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Purer is the comparative of pure, meaning cleaner or less tainted.

clue.text: Oil worker perhaps sees top of rig in free fall

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word
free fall suggests letters tumbling into a new order

explanation.surface: A man on an oil platform watches something tumble from the rig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free fall' reads as one phrase, but 'free' is fodder and 'fall' alone signals that IN and FREE are rearranged to EFINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A refiner works in oil processing, so is an example of an oil worker.

clue.text: Contribution raised from trades union —- it's not free

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards
contribution says a part of the phrase supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Union dues: a donation from a trade union, with a reminder that nothing is free.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in use is occupied or engaged, so not available.

clue.text: Painter's determination to get helper round

definitions.note: the possessive stands for painter is

indicators.note: round means the helper piece goes around the other

parts.note: a mate is an assistant, as a plumber's mate
grit is determination

explanation.surface: An artist needs resolve to bring an assistant round.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter.

clue.text: Extremely eager to bat, concealing quiet determination

indicators.note: to here means attached after, so the outer letters follow
concealing says the long outer piece hides a letter within it

parts.note: cricket bats are made of willow, so willow stands for the bat
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, outermost letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A keen cricketer hides their quiet resolve while waiting to go in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bat' looks like a verb with 'to'; it is the cricket bat, named by the wood it is made from.
explanation.definitionFit: Willpower is the strength of mind to keep going, a straight synonym for resolve.

clue.text: Cast of Falstaff originally accompanied by organ

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the Shakespeare character's name

parts.note: the lung is a body organ

explanation.surface: A theatre note about the cast of Verdi's opera Falstaff and its organ accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a noun for the actors; it is the past tense of the verb, meaning thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast is to throw, and its past tense matches the past form of fling.

clue.text: Get net out of vault

definitions.meaning: to make it as profit after costs
to ... a fence or bar is to jump over it

explanation.definitionFit: Clearing means both earning a net profit and leaping cleanly over an obstacle.

clue.text: Tiger seen roaming in national park

indicators.note: roaming suggests letters wandering about, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiger has been spotted wandering in a wildlife reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a famous national park in Tanzania, known for its wildlife.

clue.text: Conspiracy to hide pounds in teapot

indicators.note: to hide means the container keeps the small piece hidden inside it

parts.note: gunpowder is a variety of green tea, so a pot of it is a teapot
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Plotters hide their money in the teapot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunpowder Plot was the 1605 attempt to blow up the English Parliament, remembered on Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gunpowder Plot is the most famous English conspiracy, an example of the class.

clue.text: Bolster a couple of partners

parts.note: dutch is old Cockney slang for a wife, from duchess, so this is one spouse
a wife is a partner, the second of the pair

explanation.surface: Advice to support a pair of spouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolster' looks like a verb; it is a long pillow. A dutch wife is a bolster or open frame used in hot climates.
explanation.definitionFit: A dutch wife is a long bolster or cane frame for resting limbs on in bed.

clue.text: In months fortune half-squandered, going over countries

indicators.note: going over in a down clue places the first piece above the second
half-squandered means half the word is lost, keeping the front

parts.note: luck is fortune
nations are countries

explanation.surface: A gambler has spent half their fortune in months of travel abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunation is a lunar month, the time from one new moon to the next.

clue.text: Love to leave bad housing, following iron rule for building

indicators.note: following says the rearranged piece comes after the iron symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoiled and rearranged
to leave means the letter departs from the word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: Lovers quit poor accommodation, keeping to the strict letter of planning rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes the O to leave HUSING, which 'bad' rearranges. 'Love' as tennis zero is easy to miss at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Feng shui is the Chinese system of rules for placing buildings and arranging rooms.

clue.text: Charitable governors get family tree back to front

indicators.note: back to front says the second of the two pieces goes in front of the first

parts.note: the elder is a small tree
brethren are brothers, members of a family

explanation.surface: Trustees get a genealogy chart printed in the wrong order.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elder Brethren are the governing body of Trinity House, the British lighthouse and charitable corporation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elder Brethren govern Trinity House, a charitable maritime body, so the governors are named by title.

clue.text: Concerned with colour given to very big screen

parts.note: re means about or concerning
red is a colour
OS stands for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: A remark about a giant coloured screen.
explanation.walkthrough: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar; OS is the clothing-size label for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is a decorative screen standing behind an altar.

clue.text: Getting up, woman's embraced one bound to be invigorating

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue means the letters rise, read in reverse
embraced says the woman holds the second piece inside

parts.note: her refers to a woman; the 's stands for has, part of has embraced
a serf was bound to the land

explanation.surface: A woman rising from bed has hugged a servant, which feels reviving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced' gives HSERFER, and 'Getting up' turns it upwards. The 's of woman's is has, so the woman has embraced.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh is to revive or invigorate, here used without an object.

clue.text: French city gets hot

definitions.meaning: A city on the Loire in western France
makes someone hot under the collar, provokes rage

explanation.definitionFit: Angers is a French city, and the verb means infuriates or enrages.

clue.text: Suffer from tribesman, barbaric

parts.note: a Goth was one of the Germanic tribes that invaded Rome
rough and barbaric both mean crude and uncivilised

explanation.surface: Someone endures hardship at the hands of an uncivilised warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through hardship is to suffer or endure it, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Reliable type? Not quite reliable member

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: true means loyal and reliable
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Is this dependable person really a dependable politician?
explanation.definitionFit: A trump is old slang for a thoroughly good, dependable person.

clue.text: Excessive energy, supporting one of the French

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue places the letter below the rest

parts.note: un is French for one and du is French for of the
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Too much effort spent backing a French person.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means more than is warranted, hence excessive.

clue.text: Resting place to secure in good time

indicators.note: secure in says the small word is held fast inside the other piece

parts.note: a good time is fun

explanation.surface: A request to book a bed well in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style mattress used as a bed, so somewhere to rest.

clue.text: Dog starts to howl, offered unpalatable new dogfood

indicators.note: starts to points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A dog howls when given nasty new food.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound is a dog, especially one bred for hunting.

clue.text: Emphasise road leads to house

parts.note: a drive is a road, as in many street names
a home is a house

explanation.surface: Directions saying a road runs up to a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a point home is to stress it until it is understood.

clue.text: No progress here as one million rail travellers halved

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: halved keeps just the first half of the word

parts.note: people travelling by train are passengers

explanation.surface: Rail chaos: a million commuters cut by half means no progress.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a point where no further progress is possible.

clue.text: From ancient city, record monkey's run away

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: run away says the letter for run is taken out

parts.note: the rhesus is a kind of monkey; the possessive adds no letter
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A monkey escapes with a recording from an ancient site.
explanation.walkthrough: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city in what is now Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was a major ancient city of Ionia, known for its temple of Artemis.
